item.title: Weekly Food Recovery Initiative — Tue Nov 24, 2:00 PM — Blanton Hall Resident Kitchenette
item.description:
Join our weekly Food Recovery events, where dedicated volunteers and members gather to make a difference in our community. Each week, participants help collect perfectly good leftover food from Gourmet Dining and transport it to Blanton. There, the food is repackaged into individual microwavable containers and stocked in the food pantry, providing meals for those in need throughout the week. To Participate: RSVP to attend the event each week. Meet in Blanton Hall Residence Hall Kitchenette in the Communal Area (Tell them you are working with Food Recovery), Sign in via Event Pass and your set! Requirements:
Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate. Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this link. Once certified, email your certification to foodrecoverynetwork@sgamsu.org to confirm your eligibility to participate.

item.title: Inner Body Meditation (20 minutes) — Thu Dec 3, 8:30 PM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream "Awareness of the inner body takes you beyond the mind." - Eckhart Tolle
In this mediation session we will bring our attention here: to the inner body. Sessions are suitable for newcomers, those experienced in Tolle's teachings and anyone wishing to remain completely anonymous. They will last around 20 minutes and cameras and microphones will be disabled. (Depending on the situation, a free discussion may be held at the end with mics and cameras allowed.)
See you there!
Please be aware that sessions will close if no members have joined after 10 minutes.
Emrys also organises a free Work of Byron Katie online mediation group. Visit [this Meetup Group link](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/) for more information.21

item.title: In-Person and Live Stream Service — Sun Dec 6, 10:00 AM — Sanctuary
item.description:
Sunday worship takes place at 10am in person at 176 Cooper Avenue in Montclair or livestreamed on our YouTube channel: Sunday Worship Livestream Union Congregational Church is located in Montclair, New Jersey, at 176 Cooper Avenue (nearest major cross streets are Grove Street and Valley Road). There is street parking on Cooper Avenue. We have a small parking lot for seniors and those with limited mobility reached through a driveway to the left of the church. There are two accessible spots and a ramp on the left side of the building. Additional parking is available on neighboring streets. Please note that Cooper Avenue runs one way on Sundays, so it is best to enter from Valley Road or Northview Avenue. Enter the church through the main Sanctuary doors under the tower or through the accessible entrance through the Assembly Room at the top of the ramp on the left side of the church. Join Us Here Click here for the Sunday Worship Bulletin
Source: Union Congregational Church

item.title: Mah Jongg Meetup - Weekly Saturday Afternoon — Sat Dec 12, 3:00 PM — Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - Classroom
item.description:
PLEASE NOTE: You must sign up for EACH INDIVIDUAL SESSION. Signing up for one session does not register you for any following classes.
The Mah Jongg Meetup provides a weekly opportunity for players to continue practicing their established skills, sharpen their strategies, build confidence at the game table, and socialize with fellow Mah Jongg players!
The library will provide a set and table! NOTE: Attendees should already have an understanding of the Mah Jongg game. Attendees should bring their 2025 or 2026 National Mah Jongg League card to the meetup. Bringing an additional set is encouraged!
If you prefer to play the game during the week, please register for the "Mah Jongg Meetup - Weekly Thursday Morning" by clicking here
If you're new to the game, and would like to teach yourself at your own pace, please register for the "Teach Yourself Mah Jongg" by clicking here.

item.title: Hike with Dr. Kirk! 3-4 miles — Sun Dec 13, 2:00 PM
item.description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group Sunday Dec 13, 2-4:30 pm. Free expert-led hike in South Mountain Reservation. Hike about 2-3 hours covering 3-4 miles at a modest pace over rocky trails with one long climb from the Rahway River up South Mountain. Focus on ecology and hydrology, led by Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway Watershed Association and expert on local watershed issues. Good balance required. Children welcome. No dogs. Co-Sponsored by the South Mountain Conservancy and the Rahway River Watershed Association. Meet at Clipper Pavilion in South Mountain Reservation on Cherry Lane in West Orange (not at McLoone's). Steady rain cancels. Email president@rahwayriver.org with questions.
Advance registration required via [rahwayriver.org/calendar.html](rahwayriver.org/calendar.html) . Email president@rahwayriver.org with questions.

item.title: Let's Walk!! Brookdale Park — Sat Nov 28, 9:30 AM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! If entering from Bellevue Avenue and park in the first parking lot on the left. We will be gathering near the playground area.
if entering from Watchung Ave, park and walk up to the upper parking lot near the playground area.
We will be walking the outer path. There are several break-off points if you do not want to walk the entire path.
The walk will be about an hour or at least 3-4 miles.
Wear comfortable shoes!
Please plan to arrive 5 minutes early. The walk will start promptly.
Brookdale Park offers the public access to both passive and active recreational activities as well as picturesque vistas. Trails for walking and running, lush groves and extensive lawns, playgrounds, sports fields, track facilities, tennis courts, an archery range and stadium grandstand are just some of the numerous attractions that make Brookdale Park a magnet for nature lovers, families, and physical fitness enthusiasts for miles around.

item.title: DETROIT JAZZ Documentary Screening at Montclair State University FREE 6PM W/FILMMAKERS — Mon Nov 30, 6:00 PM — Montclair State University Presentation Hall College of Communications and Media
item.description: Montclair State University’s College of Communications Film Forum and the Music Department present: A Film Screening of Emerita Professor Roberta Friedman’s the new feature documentary: The Best of the Best: Jazz from Detroit with Q&A w/Filmmakers Dan Loewenthal, Roberta Friedman, and writer Stryker Monday Night November 30th, 6PM-8:45PM. at College of Communication Building’s Presentation Hall. Synopsis: The Best of the Best: Jazz from Detroit chronicles the defining impact of Detroit’s innovative and influential jazz legacy and the iconic city that produced it. Inspired by Mark Stryker’s 2019 book, Jazz from Detroit, the 90-minute documentary weaves a compelling historical and cultural tapestry through the 20th and 21st centuries. Set within Detroit’s dramatic rise and fall as an industrial power and the struggles and triumphs of its creative and resilient African American community, the film connects the dots between the city’s history and Black musical excellence.
